title: Catering, i
logline: Three weeks of strips analyzing the wedding's catering. The book takes one week. This is Tuesday.

panels.composition: Gully's. WOOD on the stool with a notebook. BARNABY in a basket on the counter now — Gully's idea. GULLY wiping.

characters.pose: in a basket on the counter

balloons.text: There were seven passed appetizers. I've ranked them.
Two and a half. The seventh was a decoy.

image.prompt: a thin man on a shop stool with an open notebook, an old dog in a basket on the counter, a stocky man wiping the counter and listening with patience, clean ink

panels.composition: The notebook: seven items, ranked, annotated in the tiny capitals he learned from her. 'gougère (adequate) · oyster (local, insulting) · something in a spoon (why)'.

image.prompt: close-up of a notebook page with a ranked list of seven wedding appetizers in cramped handwritten capitals with sarcastic annotations
image.notes: Letter after. He writes in her capitals now.

balloons.text: The cake was fine. I'll get to the cake.
Woody. You've been home three weeks and you've drawn a spoon fourteen times.
It was a very specific spoon.

image.prompt: a stocky man setting down a rag and looking at his friend with tired kindness

panels.composition: Wood, closing the notebook. Looking at the dog in the basket. The dog looking at him. The spoon, drawn once more, small, on the closed cover.
props: notebook with a small spoon drawn on the cover

image.prompt: a thin man closing a notebook on a counter and meeting the eyes of an old dog in a basket, a tiny drawing of a spoon on the notebook's cover, no words

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: Catering, week three of three. 'You've drawn a spoon fourteen times.' The dog in a basket on the counter: he can't get up on the stool anymore.
